original_question: For the range of the map A -> I(A), is the statement that the Borel hierarchy is proper with respect to that range independent of ZFC?
target_in_paper: §1 (Theodore Slaman), Problem 1(3): "Is the answer to ‘Borel hierarchy is proper w.r.t. the range of I’ independent of ZFC?", in the same problem block that first defines I(A)= {f gauge function : H^f(A) > 0}. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the relevant map A↦I(A), the descriptive-set-theoretic issue (properness of the Borel hierarchy on that range), and the metamathematical angle (possible independence from ZFC). That is exactly the content of Problem 1(3) in the Theodore Slaman section. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: The draft does not define I(A); in the paper, I(A)= {f gauge function : H^f(A) > 0}. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))

It omits the quantifier on A: the map is defined for arbitrary A ⊆ ℝ. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))

It leaves the standard notions of ‘gauge function’ and the associated Hausdorff measure H^f implicit; Problem 1 uses them without restating the definitions, so a stand-alone question should make that notation explicit. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))

It does not explicitly name the family whose complexity is at issue, namely the range {I(A) : A ⊆ ℝ}. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The phrase ‘Borel hierarchy is proper with respect to the range of I’ is not formalized in the paper, so a stand-alone rewrite should clarify that the question is whether the Borel hierarchy collapses or remains proper on this family of sets of gauge functions. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))

No regularity hypothesis on A belongs to Problem 1(3); the nearby closed-set hypothesis appears only in Problem 1(2), so importing it here would change the scope. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: For each set A ⊆ ℝ, let I(A)= {f : f is a gauge function and H^f(A) > 0}, where H^f denotes the Hausdorff measure associated with f. Is it independent of ZFC whether the Borel hierarchy is proper on the family {I(A) : A ⊆ ℝ}, equivalently in the paper’s wording, whether the Borel hierarchy is proper with respect to the range of the map A↦I(A)? ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))
justification: This paper is an open-problems compilation rather than a theorem/proposition paper, and the draft clearly targets Theodore Slaman’s Problem 1(3), not a broader neighboring issue. The same Problem 1 block first defines I(A) and then lists four ‘Natural questions about A↦I(A)’. Item (2) asks about the complexity of I(C) for closed C, showing that the surrounding context is the descriptive-set-theoretic complexity of sets of the form I(A); item (3) is exactly the ZFC-independence question in your draft. Since the paper gives no sharper equivalent reformulation for item (3), the faithful refinement is simply to restate Problem 1(3) with the hidden notation spelled out and without importing the closed-set restriction from item (2). ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))
